specialScreening.text: No official source found for extra screening of Israel flights at Schiphol (schiphol.nl blocked: owner capture). Feed: El Al, Israir and Arkia TLV departures mostly at pier G (G2, G5, G6), one at E4, KLM at D47. Time not known.

US-bound flights: TSA / DHS enhanced security measures for all last-point-of-departure airports (2017, still the baseline as far as known) may add checks at check-in or at the gate (interviews, document checks, separate screening of electronics). The procedures are not public; no time is known.

rules.text: One terminal building: departure halls 1–3 on the first floor, Schiphol Plaza with arrivals halls and the railway station on the ground floor; airside Lounges 1 (Schengen), 2 and 3 (non-Schengen) and 4 (pier M). No inter-terminal train, people mover or pier-to-pier bus: all airside movement is on foot (moving walkways). Apron buses serve remote stands only (part of boarding, see r:ams-remote-stands).
Schengen: piers B, C, M and D59–D87 (upper level of D). Non-Schengen: D1–D57 (lower level of D), E, F, G, H. Gate allocation is dynamic; the gate number decides the zone at D.

Central security since 3 June 2015: checkpoints in the departure halls (three for departing, two for transfer passengers) replaced the 130 gate lanes; there is no security at the gates of E, F, G. Extra floors on E/F/G keep unscreened arriving passengers apart.

Transfer passengers arriving from outside the EU one-stop-security area must pass a transfer security filter (central filter in the extension between piers E and F; filter on the first floor of the GH building); arrivals from e.g. the US, UK and Canada generally skip it. Not modelled per route: add ~0–30 min for such arrivals. Remediation (2026-11-01, R-05): modelled as a conditional control (when: origin-not-one-stop) on the arrivals transfer flows of piers E, F, G and H (w:ams-*-arr-l2/l3) with the one-stop list in oneStopSecurity; D (lower level) arrivals are not segregated in the model and still skip it (open). Before: Phase 3: the model cannot apply this filter to only some origins, because no control is conditional on the origin. Every arriving non-Schengen connection is therefore routed without the transfer filter, which fits passengers from one-stop-security origins only. Arrivals from other origins (most of Asia, Africa and Latin America) miss one control allowance (scenario catalogue, "missing").
Pier M (Lounge 4, Schengen low-cost) has no airside link to any other lounge or pier: connections to or from M leave through baggage claim and re-enter through security.

Pier B is reached through the temporary BC link from the root of pier C (in use since 25 Sep 2024; the old BC corridor closed for the new baggage basement). The Middenbrug Lounge 1 → B is planned to open on 18 November (year not confirmed).
Pier A (8 gates) is not in use on 2026-10-31; handover December 2026, passenger use expected April 2027. Pier C is to be rebuilt after pier A opens.

About 136 of 227 stands are remote (2025): passengers are bussed between remote stands and bus gates on the apron level (e.g. B1–B8 under pier B; a bus gate under pier D seen in 2026). The apron bus is part of the flight, not an area-to-area connection; a 2025 ride took ≈6 min.

Transfer passengers pass passport control only when changing between Schengen and non-Schengen flights (entry or exit); non-Schengen ↔ non-Schengen transfers stay in the international transit zone without passport control. Since April 2026 the EU Entry/Exit System (EES) is used for all Schengen ↔ non-Schengen transfers; self-service kiosks in the Schiphol transfer areas pre-register data. Passport allowances stay planning values (no published queue times).
KLM minimum connection time at Schiphol: 40 min Schengen ↔ Schengen, 50 min involving non-Schengen (search excerpts of klm.com transfer pages). Movement times in this model are not connection times.

Schiphol signs walking times in minutes to each pier/area ("walking times to each area posted"; guides: overhead signs quote walking times to each pier). The signed values themselves were not captured (schiphol.nl blocked; no legible sign in the frame-read videos): owner capture wanted.

The airport is open 24 hours and Holland Boulevard (Lounge 2 ↔ 3) is open 24 hours; no source gives night hours for the security, passport or transfer filters, so no walk carries opening hours and the model routes every pair at 03:00. Most airline lounges and shops close 21:00–22:00; landside Plaza areas may be limited to passengers and staff 00:00–04:00.

openQuestions.question: Does the Middenbrug (Central Bridge) Lounge 1 → pier B open on 18 November 2026 as read from the undated Schiphol news item?
openQuestions.impact: From 18 Nov 2026 Lounge 1 → B is modelled ~2 min shorter than via the BC link; if the opening slips, the status period must move.
openQuestions.howToResolve: Owner capture of schiphol.nl/en/projects/news/central-bridge-in-place (403 to automated fetch) or a dated video after 18 Nov 2026.

openQuestions.question: Is pier H reachable airside from Lounge 3/G, and are H and M two levels, two sides or the same stands? Phase 3: a 2017 first-hand blog (cultureguru.nl) says H and M "use same gates" with "access from different sides": M has its own security and entrance, and H is reached "through central security". This is consistent with the modelled L3 ↔ H walk. The exact airside path from Lounge 3 and the current (2026) arrangement are still unconfirmed.
openQuestions.impact: H ↔ other non-Schengen piers is routed airside via Lounge 3 (probable); if H is isolated like M, those routes must go landside.
openQuestions.howToResolve: Official terminal map (owner capture), or a dated walkthrough of the H gates.

sources.title: Schiphol: All about your transfer at Schiphol
sources.notes: Text copied by the owner 2026-11-02 (schiphol.nl blocks automated access). No repeat security after flights from the US, Canada, UK, Ireland, Singapore, Cyprus, Serbia (only flights from Belgrade) and Schengen countries; Schengen ↔ non-Schengen transfers need passport control; Schengen → non-Schengen may also need security. Official video of the same date: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BAqxZ3TztkU (arrival → transfer security → Lounge 2 → passport e-gates → Lounge 1).

sources.title: Schiphol: opening hours of the security filters (departure filters 1, 1a, 2, 3, M; transfer filters EF and GH; Schengen and arrival passport filters)
sources.notes: Table copied by the owner from official Schiphol information on 2026-11-02 (schiphol.nl blocks automated access; exact page URL to be recorded). Transfer Filter EF 24/7; Transfer Filter GH 04:30–23:30; Departure Filter 1 and 3 24/7, 1a 04:00–end of operations, 2 05:15–end of operations (Sat/Sun from 06:00), M 05:00–21:30 depending on the schedule; Arrival Schengen (NS/S) 24/7; Departures Schengen (S/NS) 05:00–22:00 incl. T-passage for crew and PRM; Arrival Filters 1 and 3 06:00–21:30, 2 and 4 24/7. Applied: EF and GH (their positions are named in the model). The other filters await a verified physical mapping.

sources.title: Amsterdam Airport Schiphol (Wikipedia)
sources.notes: Low weight. Piers B, C, M Schengen; E, F, G, H non-Schengen; D both on separate levels; D59–D87 via Departure Hall 1; pier A under construction, expected April 2027, 8 gates; 227 stands in 2025 (91 contact, 136 remote); Lounge 1 expansion completed Nov 2024; G9, E18, E24 A380-capable.

sources.title: Schiphol Airport (Wikivoyage)
sources.notes: Lounge 1 (Schengen): B, C, D59–D87 (escalator up from Lounge 1); Lounge 2: E and D3–D57; Lounge 3: F, G, H; Lounge 4: M only, fully separated; Lounge 1 → 2/3 needs immigration; M connections must exit via baggage claim; station under Schiphol Plaza.

sources.title: Schiphol Terminal Guide: Departure Halls, Piers and Lounges
sources.notes: One terminal, departure halls 1–3; D two levels (D59–D87 Schengen, lower numbers non-Schengen); H non-Schengen low-cost, M Schengen low-cost and isolated; pier A not open in 2026, expected April 2027; Lounges 2 and 3 linked to Lounge 1; ~20 min hall → far G gate.

sources.title: Greater comfort as a result of central security
sources.notes: Central security from 3 June 2015: five central checkpoints (three for departing, two for transfer passengers) replace 130 gate lanes; extra level on piers E, F, G to separate flows.

sources.title: Great engineering on Airside (B-C link)
sources.notes: 270 m corridor B–C on poles 4 m above the apron, 8 modules; "Pier B will only be accessible temporarily through this corridor due to the construction of the new terminal".

sources.title: Schiphol opens new area: much more space for passengers in Lounge 1
sources.notes: 5,000 m² new Lounge 1 section for European flights; new walking route; renewal of pier C listed as a planned project.
